A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GERNE, with matching authors, research objectives, and experiments. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original GERNE benchmark results, hyperparameter experiments in Figures 2–3, and validation-only training experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports revised GERNE results on bFFHQ in Table 1.

M1.justification: The batch construction, extrapolated gradient, and pseudo-attribute mechanism remain unchanged. However, v2 Algorithm 2 explicitly permits beta above the known-attribute upper bound, whereas v1 simply invokes Algorithm 1 and its Eq. (9) constraint. This is a limited revision to the stated unknown-attribute training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate C-MNIST, C-CIFAR-10, bFFHQ, Waterbirds, CelebA, and CivilComments, retaining the minority-ratio settings, attribute-availability scenarios, and Appendix G experiments. Expanded dataset descriptions do not establish additional coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds reported DeNetDM comparisons for all four C-CIFAR-10 minority ratios and bFFHQ in Table 1. Its C-MNIST results are explicitly excluded because the dataset version differs. Resampling is the renamed existing GERNE configuration with c=1 and beta=0; Table 2 and Appendix G retain their comparators.

E3.justification: v2 specifies grid search and adopts -1 as the known-attribute beta search lower limit, replacing v1's general Eq. (9) constraint and recommended starting pair. Algorithm 2 also explicitly relaxes the unknown-attribute upper limit. Other reported architectures, optimization settings, metrics, and cross-validation procedures remain unchanged; these revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Figures 2–3 retain the same beta and threshold experiments and findings. Appendix G retains the validation-only and cross-validation analyses. The sampling-and-weighting variance comparison moves from Appendix C to B; the new bound derivation supplies theoretical analysis rather than a new empirical ablation.

E5.justification: v2 adds a Table 3 caption describing standard deviations over three trials, although its retained cross-validation paragraph specifies nine runs, as in v1. This introduces a reporting inconsistency, not evidence of fewer runs. The three-trial reporting in Tables 1–2 and seed information in Figure 2 otherwise remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises bFFHQ accuracy: known-attribute GERNE changes from 77.10±0.90 to 85.20±0.86, unknown-attribute GERNE from 70.87±0.61 to 76.80±1.21, and Resampling from 69.80±1.33 to 72.13±0.90. DeNetDM entries are added. Other retained benchmark values and Tables 2–3 are unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the bFFHQ revisions.

T1.justification: New Appendix C proves a simplified upper bound determined by the largest conditional group proportion and chooses -1 as the tuning lower limit. Section 4.1.5 also corrects the minority-weighting argument by specifying beta>1/c-1. The foundational distribution, variance, and pseudo-attribute arguments are retained.

C1.justification: v2 removes the abstract and introduction's claim that the bounds ensure convergence and drops the explicit identification of reweighting as an encompassed special case. The central gradient-extrapolation contribution, known/unknown attribute applicability, and six-benchmark performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation linking beta sensitivity to the bound's dependence on c and A, and suggests augmentation explains LC's small advantage on C-MNIST at 5%. It removes v1's explicit conclusion limitation concerning insufficient use of majority-group diversity. The discussion of validation imbalance and attribute availability remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and more explicit pseudocode and tuning instructions. Conversely, Appendix F.1 no longer specifies v1's discrete c candidates {1/2,1} for known-attribute experiments. Architectures, learning rates, batch sizes, optimizer settings, and preprocessing details are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: DeNetDM is newly cited and incorporated into the experimental comparison. The broader positioning against group-robustness and balancing approaches remains stable. Other reference changes principally update bibliographic metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodological explanations, experimental discussion, and conclusion undergo widespread rewriting. Six contribution bullets become three, dataset explanations expand, the resampling discussion moves from Appendix B into Section 5.1, and the mathematical appendices are reorganized. This substantially revises exposition despite largely retained scientific content.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables are resized or restyled, Table 1 gains a DeNetDM row, and Table 3 replaces its boxed grid with a cleaner format. Figure 3 uses scaled threshold labels and an expanded caption; Table 1 and Algorithm 1 move. The same three figures, three tables, and two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition, the additional bound derivation, correction of the minority-weighting condition, and removal of the unproved convergence guarantee modestly improve precision and usability. DeNetDM also strengthens comparison coverage. These benefits are tempered by omitted c-search details, removal of an explicit limitation, and inconsistent Table 3 trial reporting. The unexplained bFFHQ score increases do not themselves establish improved paper quality.
